content:
maria: Quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak the prefix cache hit-rate dropped on our chat workloads with long contexts. Seeing ~12% absolute hit-rate regression on the customer RAG test-suite (avg seq ~1024). Profiling attached below.

aj: Oh no. Which kernel change exactly?

maria: We landed a heuristic that prefers the fused-attn fallback on Ampere when sequence > 768 to avoid memory spikes. It reduces memory but I think it alters KV layout and invalidates some key normalization assumptions.

shelly: Can you paste the slow path trace? :eyes:

maria: Sure — this is from redwood-prof on the canary run (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-15T18:02:33Z] redwood-prof: route=chat-rag, model=xlarge-v2, seq=1024
  kv_lookup  14.2%  (expected ~3-5%)
  kv_build   33.8%
  kernel_swap 18.4%
  batching_overhead  9.7%
  attention_fallback  12.1%
  prefix_cache_miss  11.8%  (was 0.5-1.5% baseline)
```

ryan: prefix_cache_miss that high is wild. Are keys actually different or are we evicting earlier?
devon: I instrumented key fingerprints for a sample of conversations. Before the change ~92% of top-100 prefixes had identical fingerprints across models/instances. After the change only ~77% matched — the hash space got polluted by sequence-chunking differences.
aj: Sequence-chunking differences as in we changed how we split long prompts for fused-attn? That's plausible — different chunk sizes -> different prefix boundaries -> different key digests.
maria: Exactly. The fused-attn path pads/aligns chunks to 64 for better kernels; that alters the token offsets we use in cache key generation. Two things happening: key variance + our eviction policy (LRU with time-windows tuned for smaller sequences) means higher churn.
shelly: Two quick mitigations we can try in parallel: 1) normalize keys to ignore chunk-alignment padding and 2) extend affinity window so a convo's working set sticks to the same GPU for longer (reduce cross-GPU misses).

maria: I'm already prototyping key normalization. Pseudocode: 
```python
# naive normalization idea
def normalize_prefix_key(tokens, seq_len, padding_alignment=64):
    # strip trailing pad tokens introduced by fused-attn chunk aligner
    end = len(tokens) - (len(tokens) % padding_alignment)
    if end < len(tokens):
        trimmed = tokens[:end] + ["<ALIGN>"]
    else:
        trimmed = tokens
    # stable fingerprint across minor chunking differences
    return sha256(" ".join(trimmed)).hexdigest()
```
This collapses boundaries but still encodes a signal for alignment differences.

ryan: Nice. Also, can batching coalescing be causing false collisions? If different convs are batched and we canonicalize keys too coarsely we might be attributing a batch's KV to the wrong convo.
devon: Good point. I checked the batching logs: we do dynamic coalescing when qps spikes — it's merging requests with similar seq distributions. In theory that's fine, but we tag KV namespaces with the job-id not conversation-id when coalesced. That was an optimization to reduce metadata overhead. That will break per-convo cache semantics.
aj: So two vectors: key variance from chunking and namespace weakening from batch coalescing. Both increase misses. Proposed short-term plan:
- Revert the job-id namespace optimization for coalesced batches (hotfix).
- Deploy key normalization v1 that strips alignment padding.
- Increase affinity_window from 60s -> 300s for chat-heavy routes.

shelly: Long-term: we should make kernel selection emit a stable token-offset transform that the cache keyer can consume (i.e., a deterministic alignment map) rather than implicit side-effects. Kernel metadata should include `alignment_map` and `padding_policy`.

perf-bot: Canary run scheduled: canary-2003460000 will run with: revert-batch-namespace + keynorm-v1 + affinity-300s. Will report after 30m.

maria: Also adding an eval harness: compare top-500 prefixes hit-rate for chat vs completion vs RAG in 15-min rolling windows. Baseline (pre-change): chat=88%, completion=94%, RAG=78%. Current (post-change): chat=76%, completion=92%, RAG=65%.

ryan: Those deltas line up with the chunking hypothesis — RAG suffers more since doc offsets + retrieval chunks produce more boundary sensitivity.

devon: For warmup strategies, let's test three approaches:
1) client-side sticky affinity (stick convo to GPU for X minutes)
2) synthetic prefix prefetch: server replays top-k prefixes for a route after deploy to prepopulate caches
3) probabilistic read-through: on miss, do a cheap speculative partial KV build to pre-warm adjacent prefixes.

shelly: Synthetic prefetch seems effective for steady-state traffic (low churn customers), but for PLG interactive chat it's expensive. Probabilistic read-through might be best default (cheap partial builds).

maria: Agree. For the canary I'll enable 2 & 3 only for the canary route (redwood/canary/chat-rag) and metric collection.

aj: One more ask: add an automated diff check for key entropy when we change kernels — if normalized key cardinality deviates >5% we should block auto-rollout.

maria: Good call. I'll draft a PR for the key-normalizer + gating check.

perf-bot: Canary finished: preliminary results (30m): prefix hit-rate: chat=86% (+10), completion=93% (+1), RAG=76% (+11). KV build time reduced 28%. No abnormal mem spikes.

maria: Great — rollback not needed. I'll follow up with a proper postmortem and add kernel->key contract in the spec. Thanks all. :tada:
